content.title: President Trump to give speech today about Iran war. When is it?
content.text: Updated April 1, 2026, 7:30 p.m. CTPresident Donald Trump will give an update on the Iran war on Wednesday, April 1, according to White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt.The news comes after Trump shared an updated timeline for the end of the war on Tuesday, telling reporters in the Oval Office that he expects it to be over within "two weeks, maybe three.""I would say within two weeks, maybe, two weeks, maybe three," Trump said when asked about how much longer it would take for the war to end. "I think within two or three weeks, we’ll leave. There’s no reason for us to do this."Here's how to watch Trump's address to the nation on Wednesday, April 1.What time is Trump speaking today?Trump's address to the nation will take place at 8 p.m. CT on Wednesday, April 1, according to a social media post from Leavitt.How can I watch Trump's address to the nation tonight?Most major news channels, like NBC, ABC, CBS, FOX, PBS, CNN, MS NOW, FOX News, NewsNation and many others, are covering the speech, so you can livestream the address online with a subscription to DirecTV, Fubo, Hulu + Live TV, Sling and other cable providers.The Des Moines Register and USA TODAY Network Iowa websites will carry the speech live on their websites and apps. It is also available on the USA TODAY YouTube channel.How is the war with Iran affecting Iowans?The war with Iran is driving fertilizer and fuel costs higher for Iowa and other U.S. farmers, who already are struggling with a fourth year of expected losses.The price spike also is raising concerns about higher grocery bills for consumers. Some farmers said prices are as much as 40% higher than they were last fall. When farmers face supply shortages or major price spikes, "those impacts ripple through the entire food chain” resulting in “higher prices for our families across America,” said Zippy Duvall, president of the Farm Bureau, who raises chickens and beef cattle in Georgia. Iowans killed in Iran warSix soldiers from the Des Moines-based 103rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command were killed in an Iranian attack on March 1 in Kuwait. Two Des Moines-area residents and one former West Des Moines resident were among those killed.Maj. Jeffrey O'Brien, 45, was a father of three from Waukee. Sgt. Declan Coady, 20, was a graduate of Dowling Catholic High School and was studying at Drake University.Chief Warrant Officer 3 Robert Marzan grew up in Sacramento, California, but lived in West Des Moines from 2007 to 2023.Capt. Cody A. Khork, Sgt. 1st Class Nicole M. Amor and Sgt. 1st Class Noah L. Tietjens were also among the first casualties in the Iran War.Des Moines Register reporter Donnelle Eller and Kyle Werner contributed to this article, as well as USA Today reporters Christopher Cann, Bart Jansen, Cybele Mayes-Osterman, Michael Loria, Rachel Barber and Zac Anderson.Lucia Cheng is a service and trending reporter at the Des Moines Register. Contact her at lcheng@gannett.com or 515-284-8132.
